name: Chain of Draft (CoD)
executive_summary: Forces intermediate reasoning steps to a strict word limit (typically ≤5 words per step), matching or exceeding CoT accuracy while reducing token generation by up to 90%.
description: Inspired by human cognitive shorthand, CoD instructs the model to think step by step but keep only a minimum draft for each thinking step. Each draft step is capped at a configurable word count. The final answer is returned after a separator (e.g., ####). Works best on capable models.
when_to_use: Token cost is a binding constraint and you need step-by-step reasoning.
The target model is capable (≥7B parameters).
Tasks involve arithmetic, logic, or multi-step deduction.
when_not_to_use: Model is small (<3B) and may misinterpret ultra-concise drafts.
The reasoning trace itself is a deliverable.
known_pitfalls: Smaller models may produce ambiguous or incomplete drafts.
The separator must be clearly distinguished from reasoning content.
Draft length hyperparameter may need tuning per task.

primary_source.title: Chain of Draft: Thinking Faster by Writing Less

variables.name: max_words
variables.description: Maximum words allowed per reasoning draft step.

variables.name: problem_statement
variables.description: The problem or question to solve.
variables.example: If a train travels 60 km in 30 minutes, how far will it travel in 2 hours at the same speed?

usage_templates.reproducibility_note: A single LLM call with explicit formatting constraints. Output length varies by problem complexity but is bounded by max_words * estimated_steps.
